dish.title: Cajun Blackened Catfish with Herb Remoulade

recipe_version.title: Cajun Blackened Catfish with Herb Remoulade
recipe_version.description: Catfish fillets coated in Cajun blackening spices and seared hard in a hot skillet, served with a dairy-free herb remoulade.

ingredients.name: catfish fillets
ingredients.note: 4 fillets, about 6 oz each, skinless. Pat dry. Finfish.

ingredients.name: cayenne pepper
ingredients.note: heat in the rub; reduce to 1/2 tsp for milder

ingredients.name: kosher salt
ingredients.note: divided: 1 tsp in the rub, 1/4 tsp in the remoulade

ingredients.name: black pepper
ingredients.note: divided: 1/2 tsp in the rub, 1/4 tsp in the remoulade

ingredients.name: neutral oil
ingredients.note: divided: 2 tbsp for blackening the fish (may need a second spoon if cooking in two batches), 1 tbsp whisked into the remoulade base with the mayo

ingredients.name: egg mayonnaise
ingredients.note: HARD DAIRY-FREE CONTRACT. Use classic egg mayonnaise made from oil and egg (or a labeled dairy-free mayo). Do not use buttermilk, yogurt, sour cream, or any mayo that lists milk. No dairy mayo ambiguity.

ingredients.name: Dijon mustard
ingredients.note: for the remoulade. Typical Dijon is mustard seed and vinegar without wheat; confirm label. Not honey mustard.

ingredients.name: dill pickle relish
ingredients.note: drained. Or finely chopped dill pickle. Built remoulade component, not a bottled remoulade.

ingredients.name: hot sauce
ingredients.note: vinegar-pepper sauce such as a classic cayenne hot sauce. No butter-based hot sauce.

steps.title: Mix the blackening rub and make the remoulade
steps.body: Stir together the sweet paprika, cayenne, garlic powder, onion powder, dried thyme, dried oregano, 1 tsp of the kosher salt, and 1/2 tsp of the black pepper. In a separate bowl, whisk the egg mayonnaise with the Dijon mustard, lemon juice, 1 tbsp of the neutral oil, dill pickle relish, chopped capers, parsley, chives, garlic paste, hot sauce, the remaining 1/4 tsp kosher salt, and the remaining 1/4 tsp black pepper. This herb remoulade is made here. It is not a bottled remoulade. Confirm the mayonnaise has no milk, buttermilk, or cream. Chill the remoulade while the fish cooks. Pat the catfish fillets dry.

steps.title: Coat the catfish
steps.body: Press both sides of each catfish fillet into the blackening rub so the spices adhere in an even coat. Shake off only the loosest excess. Do not flour the fish. Do not egg-wash it. Do not bread it.

steps.title: Blacken in a hot skillet
steps.body: Heat a 12-inch cast-iron or heavy stainless skillet over medium-high until it is very hot, about 3 minutes. Add 2 tbsp of the neutral oil and swirl. Lay in as many fillets as fit without crowding (often 2). Cook undisturbed until the spice crust is darkened and fragrant and the edges look opaque, about 3 to 4 minutes. Flip once. Cook the second side about 3 to 4 minutes more, until the thickest part flakes and is opaque (about 145 F if checked). Move cooked fillets to a warm plate. Add a thin film of the remaining oil if the pan is dry and cook the remaining fillets the same way. The written clock uses one 3-minute preheat plus two batches of about 7 minutes each (14) overlapping the plate-hold; cook_minutes below uses 17 for preheat + batch work. Do not deep-fry. Do not bake. kitchen_tested is false.

steps.title: Plate with remoulade
steps.body: Serve each blackened catfish fillet with a spoonful of the dairy-free herb remoulade on the side or a stripe on the plate. No butter basting. No buttermilk soak. No nuts. No breaded coating.

recipe_version.heat: Skillet preheated over medium-high until very hot. Blacken over medium-high. No oven. No grill required.
recipe_version.doneness: Spice crust darkened (blackened) and fragrant, not raw-spice pale and not incinerated ash. Fish opaque and flakes at the thickest point, about 145 F. Remoulade cold and spoonable. kitchen_tested is false.

dietary_eligibility.nut_policy_note: No peanuts, tree nuts, or cashews. Capers and spices are not nuts.
dietary_eligibility.hh001_reason: Finfish (catfish) is allowed for HH001. Remoulade is hard-contracted dairy-free (egg mayo, no buttermilk). No shellfish, no meat other than fish, no poultry, no nuts. Egg mayo is allowed; eggs are permitted for HH001.

recipe_version.dietary_label_note: Unconditional dairy_free. The remoulade uses egg mayonnaise with no milk, buttermilk, yogurt, sour cream, or cream. This is not a skip-the-butter version of a dairy remoulade. Finfish is present, so this is not plant-based or vegetarian.
allergen_notes: Egg covers the egg mayonnaise in the remoulade. If a cook used a labeled egg-free dairy-free mayo instead, egg would drop; this written package uses egg mayonnaise and lists egg.

Dijon mustard is not a major allergen token in this factory token set. Typical Dijon has no wheat; confirm the bottle. No soy, wheat, sesame, peanut, tree_nut, shellfish, or milk in the written ingredients.

scaling_notes.1: One 6 oz catfish fillet. Rub: about 1.5 tsp total spice mix (still enough cayenne for a true blacken). Remoulade floor: 2 tbsp egg mayo, 1 tsp Dijon, 1 tsp lemon, 1 tsp relish, 1 tsp herbs, pinch salt — do not quarter into a smear that disappears. Oil: 2 tsp in the skillet. Same hot-skillet method; no batching.
scaling_notes.2: Two fillets (about 12 oz). Half the rub and remoulade. One batch in the skillet. Halve the oil.
scaling_notes.4: As written. Four fillets, likely two batches in a 12-inch skillet.

coverage_contribution: Opens Cajun/Southern cuisine (0 live). Catfish is an unused finfish species in a salmon/cod-heavy catalog. Blackened spice crust is a different texture from battered fish tacos or lemon-herb fillets. Dairy-free remoulade keeps HH001 eligibility.
near_duplicate_review: Compared with Crispy Fish Tacos: both are finfish, but tacos are battered/fried-style with cabbage slaw and Mexican format; this is blackened catfish with remoulade, plated fillet, Cajun spice. Compared with Maple-Mustard Glazed Salmon and Miso-Ginger Salmon: different species and glaze vs blackened crust. Compared with Ginger-Scallion Fish Packets and Citrus-Fennel Arctic Char: packet/steam and Scandinavian roast, not Cajun skillet. Compared with Grilled Swordfish Olive Caper: grilled Mediterranean, not blackened Cajun. Compared with Garlic-Tomato Mussels / Lemon-Garlic Shrimp Pasta: shellfish — deliberately avoided. Not shrimp and grits.
